translations.literal: An order was issued for the Nine Ministers to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to deliberate and carry this out.

sentences.zh: 大學士英祀京師賢良祠，复即本籍諭祭，命廷玉歸行禮，並令子若靄從；

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ying was enshrined in the Worthies Shrine in the capital; an edict was also issued for sacrifice at his native place, and Tingyu was ordered to return to perform the rites, his son Ruowei also commanded to accompany him;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ying was enshrined in the Worthies Shrine in the capital, and sacrifice was also ordered at his native place; Zhang Tingyu was sent home to perform the rites, with his son Ruowei accompanying him;

sentences.zh: 弟廷璐督江蘇學政，亦命來會。

translations.literal: his brother Tinglu, supervising educational commissioner of Jiangsu, was also ordered to attend.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Tinglu, Jiangsu educational commissioner, was also summoned to join them.

sentences.zh: 發帑金萬為英建祠，並賜冠帶、衣裘及貂皮、人參、內府書籍五十二種。

translations.literal: Ten thousand taels from the treasury were disbursed to build a shrine for Ying, and there were also bestowed official hat and belt, fur garments, sable pelts, ginseng, and fifty-two kinds of books from the imperial library.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand taels from the treasury were allocated to build Ying a shrine, along with grants of official regalia, fur robes, sable pelts, ginseng, and fifty-two kinds of books from the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 十二月，廷玉疏言：「行經直隸，被水諸縣已予賑，尚有積潦不能種麥，請敕加賑一月。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Tingyu memorialized: "Passing through Zhili, the flood-stricken counties have already received relief, but standing water still prevents sowing wheat; he requested an edict for one month's additional relief."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhang Tingyu memorialized: "Traveling through Zhili, I found flood-hit counties already under relief, but standing water still prevents wheat planting; I ask that relief be extended one month."

sentences.zh: 並議以工代賑。

translations.literal: It was also deliberated to use work in place of relief.
translations.idiomatic: Relief-through-labor was also proposed.

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: The imperial rescript approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，還京師，上遣內大臣、侍郎海望迎勞盧溝橋，賜酒膳。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year he returned to the capital; the emperor sent an inner minister and Vice Minister Haiwang to welcome and greet him at the Lugou Bridge and bestowed wine and a feast.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year he returned to the capital; the emperor sent an inner minister and Vice Minister Haiwang to greet him at the Lugou Bridge with wine and a feast.

sentences.zh: 十三年，世宗疾大漸，與大學士鄂爾泰等同被顧命。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, as the Shizong Emperor's illness grew grave, he and Grand Secretary Oertai were together entrusted with the regency.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, as Emperor Shizong's illness worsened, he and Grand Secretary Oertai were named regents.

sentences.zh: 遺詔以廷玉器量純全，抒誠供職，命他日配享太廟。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict praised Tingyu's character as pure and whole and his sincere discharge of duty, and ordered that he be granted posthumous sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple in due course.
translations.idiomatic: The deathbed edict praised Zhang Tingyu's unsullied character and loyal service and commanded that he someday receive posthumous enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，命總理事務，予世職一等阿達哈哈番，合為三等子，仍以若靄襲。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor ascended the throne, he was ordered to take overall charge of affairs; a hereditary first-class adaha guardsman title was granted, combined into a third-rank zi, still to be inherited by Ruowei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Zhang Tingyu was put in overall charge of affairs and granted a hereditary first-class adaha guardsman title combined into a third-rank zi, with Ruowei still to inherit.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，明史成，表進，命仍兼管翰林院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Qianlong reign the History of Ming was completed and presented in a memorial; he was ordered still to oversee Hanlin Academy affairs concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the History of Ming was completed and presented; he was told to continue overseeing the Hanlin Academy as well.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，辭總理事務，加拜他喇布勒哈番，特命與鄂爾泰同進三等伯，賜號勤宣，仍以若靄襲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year he resigned from overall charge of affairs; he was additionally invested as tabuha guardsman, specially ordered together with Oertai to be promoted to third-rank count, granted the style Qinxuan, still to be inherited by Ruowei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year he resigned from overall charge; he was further invested as tabuha guardsman and, by special order, promoted with Oertai to third-rank count and granted the honorific Qinxuan, with Ruowei still to inherit.

sentences.zh: 四年，加太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was granted Senior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Senior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 尋諭：「本朝文臣無爵至侯伯者，廷玉為例外，命自兼，不必令若靄襲。」

translations.literal: Soon an edict stated: "In this dynasty no civil official's ennoblement has reached marquis or count; Tingyu is an exception—the title is ordered to be held concurrently by himself, without requiring Ruowei to inherit."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor declared: "No civil official in this dynasty has been ennobled to marquis or count rank; Zhang Tingyu is the exception—let him hold the title himself, without requiring Ruowei to inherit."

sentences.zh: 又諭：「廷玉年已過七十，不必向早入朝，炎暑風雪無強入。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Tingyu is already past seventy; he need not attend court early, and in heat or snow he is not compelled to attend."
translations.idiomatic: He was also told: "Zhang Tingyu is past seventy—he need not come to court early, and need not attend in extreme heat or snow."

sentences.zh: 十一年，若靄卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Ruowei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Ruowei died.

sentences.zh: 上以廷玉入內廷須扶掖，命次子庶吉士若澄直南書房。

translations.literal: Because the emperor saw that Tingyu needed support entering the inner court, he ordered the second son, Hanlin bachelor Ruocheng, to serve in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Zhang Tingyu needed assistance entering the inner court, the emperor posted his second son Ruocheng, a Hanlin bachelor, to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以老病乞休。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, citing old age and illness, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he asked to retire on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「卿受兩朝厚恩，且奉皇考遺命配享太廟，豈有從祀元臣歸田終老？」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "You have received deep favor from two reigns, and bear my late father's testamentary command of enshrinement in the Ancestral Temple—how can a minister enshrined alongside the throne retire to the countryside to end his days?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "You owe deep debt to two reigns, and my late father's edict names you for Ancestral Temple enshrinement—how can a minister honored for posthumous sacrifice retire to farm his fields?"

sentences.zh: 廷玉言：「宋、明配享諸臣亦有乞休得請者。

translations.literal: Tingyu said: "In Song and Ming, ministers granted posthumous sacrifice also petitioned for retirement and were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu answered: "In Song and Ming times, ministers honored for posthumous sacrifice also asked to retire and were allowed.

sentences.zh: 且七十懸車，古今通義。」

translations.literal: Moreover, at seventy to hang up one's carriage is a principle honored in every age."
translations.idiomatic: And retiring at seventy is a principle honored in every age."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 易稱見幾而作，非所論於國家關休戚、視君臣為一體者。

translations.literal: The Changes speaks of acting when one sees the turning point—this is not what applies when the state's fortune is at stake and ruler and minister are one body.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes speaks of retiring when one sees the turning point—but that does not apply when the state's welfare hangs in the balance and ruler and minister are one body.

sentences.zh: 使七十必令懸車，何以尚有八十杖朝之典？

translations.literal: If at seventy one must necessarily hang up one's carriage, why is there still the precedent of court audience with staff at eighty?
translations.idiomatic: If retirement were mandatory at seventy, why does the tradition of attending court with a staff at eighty still stand?

sentences.zh: 武侯鞠躬盡瘁，又何為耶？」

translations.literal: The Marquis of Wu bowed until his strength was spent—what was that for?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang wore himself out in service—what was that for?"

sentences.zh: 廷玉又言：「亮受任軍旅，臣幸得優游太平，未可同日而語。」

translations.literal: Tingyu said again: "Liang received charge amid armies on campaign; I have been fortunate to enjoy ease in a time of peace—they cannot be spoken of in the same breath."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu replied: "Liang served at the head of armies in wartime; I have been lucky to serve in peaceful ease—they are not comparable."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「是又不然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That too is not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That too is wrong.

sentences.zh: 皋、夔、龍、比易地皆然。

translations.literal: Gao Yao, Kui, Long, and Bi would be the same if positions were exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yao, Kui, Long, and Bi would act the same in each other's roles.

sentences.zh: 既以身任天下之重，則不以艱鉅自諉，亦豈得以承平自逸？

translations.literal: Once one has taken upon oneself the weight of the realm, one does not shirk because tasks are arduous, nor may one take ease because times are peaceful?
translations.idiomatic: Once you shoulder the weight of empire, you do not beg off because the burden is heavy—nor may you slacken because times are peaceful?

sentences.zh: 朕為卿思之，不獨受皇祖、皇考優渥之恩，不可言去；

translations.literal: I think of this for you: not only have you received generous favor from my grandfather and my late father—you cannot speak of leaving;
translations.idiomatic: Consider this: you owe more than generous debt to my grandfather and late father—you cannot speak of leaving;

sentences.zh: 即以朕十餘年眷待，亦不當言去。

translations.literal: even setting aside my more than ten years of affectionate treatment, you still ought not speak of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: to say nothing of more than ten years of my own favor—you still ought not speak of leaving.

sentences.zh: 朕且不忍令卿去，卿顧能辭朕去耶？

translations.literal: I cannot bear to let you go—can you bring yourself to refuse me and go?
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to let you go—how can you insist on leaving me?

sentences.zh: 朕謂致仕之義，必古人遭逢不偶，不得已之苦衷。

translations.literal: I hold that the meaning of retirement must be the bitter necessity of ancients who met ill fortune and had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that retirement was meant for ancients who met ill fortune and had no alternative.

sentences.zh: 為人臣者，設預存此心，必將漠視一切，泛泛如秦、越，年至則奉身以退，誰復出力為國家治事？

translations.literal: For a minister, if one premeditates such a mind, one will necessarily disregard everything, drift apart like Qin and Yue, and at the proper age withdraw oneself—who then will exert effort to govern affairs for the state?
translations.idiomatic: A minister who nurses such a thought will treat duty lightly, drift apart like strangers, and retire when age permits—then who will do the work of state?

sentences.zh: 是不可以不辨。」

translations.literal: This cannot go unclarified."
translations.idiomatic: This must be clarified."

sentences.zh: 因命舉所諭宣告朝列，並允廷玉解兼管吏部，廷玉自是不敢言去。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered that what had been instructed be proclaimed to the court, and also permitted Tingyu to relinquish concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel; Tingyu himself no longer dared speak of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered these words proclaimed to the court, granted Zhang Tingyu release from concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel, and Zhang Tingyu no longer dared speak of leaving.

sentences.zh: 然廷玉實老病，十四年正月，命如宋文彥博十日一至都堂議事，四五日一入內廷備顧問。

translations.literal: Yet Tingyu was truly aged and ill; in the first month of the fourteenth year he was ordered, like Song Wen Yanbo, to come to the capital yamen once every ten days to deliberate on affairs, and to enter the inner court every four or five days as consultant.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhang Tingyu was genuinely old and ill; in the first month of the fourteenth year he was allowed, like Song Wen Yanbo, to attend the capital yamen every ten days for deliberation and enter the inner court every four or five days as consultant.

sentences.zh: 是冬，廷玉乞休沐養疴，上命解所兼領監修、總裁諸職，且令軍機大臣往省。

translations.literal: That winter Tingyu requested leave to recuperate; the emperor ordered him relieved of all concurrent posts as supervising compiler and chief editor, and also ordered Grand Councilors to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhang Tingyu asked leave to convalesce; the emperor relieved him of his concurrent supervising-editor posts and sent Grand Councilors to visit him.

sentences.zh: 廷玉言：「受上恩不敢言去，私意原得暫歸。

translations.literal: Tingyu said: "Having received the emperor's grace I dare not speak of leaving, but in private I had hoped to return home temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu said: "Having received your grace I dare not speak of leaving, but I had hoped in private to return home for a time.

sentences.zh: 後年，上南巡，當於江寧迎駕。」

translations.literal: The year after next, when the emperor tours south, he would meet the imperial progress at Jiangning."
translations.idiomatic: The year after next, when Your Majesty tours the south, I would meet you at Jiangning."

sentences.zh: 上乃許廷玉致仕，命待來春冰泮，舟行歸里。

translations.literal: The emperor then granted Tingyu retirement and ordered him to wait until the ice melted the following spring and return home by boat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then granted Zhang Tingyu retirement and told him to wait until the ice broke the following spring and go home by boat.

sentences.zh: 親制詩三章以賜，廷玉入謝，奏言：「蒙世宗遺命配享太廟，上年奉恩諭，從祀元臣不宜歸田終老，恐身後不獲更蒙大典。

translations.literal: The emperor personally composed three poems as gifts; Tingyu entered to give thanks and memorialized: "By Shizong's testamentary command I was granted Ancestral Temple sacrifice; last year, receiving the gracious edict that a minister enshrined alongside the throne should not retire to the countryside, I feared that after death I would not again receive the great honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote three poems as gifts; Zhang Tingyu came to give thanks and said: "Emperor Shizong's edict promised me Ancestral Temple sacrifice; last year Your Majesty's gracious word held that a minister honored for posthumous enshrinement should not retire to the fields—I feared that after death I might not receive that honor after all.

sentences.zh: 免冠叩首，乞上一言為券。」

translations.literal: Removing his hat he kowtowed, begging the emperor for a word as pledge."
translations.idiomatic: He doffed his hat, kowtowed, and begged a word from the emperor as pledge."

sentences.zh: 上意不懌，然猶為頒手詔，申世宗成命，並製詩示意，以明劉基乞休後仍配享為例。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, yet still issued a personal edict reaffirming Shizong's established command and composed a poem to make his intent clear, citing Liu Ji's retirement followed still by posthumous sacrifice as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased but still issued a personal edict reaffirming Shizong's command and wrote a poem clarifying his intent, citing Liu Ji's retirement yet posthumous enshrinement as precedent.

sentences.zh: 次日，遣子若澄入謝。

translations.literal: The next day he sent his son Ruocheng to enter and give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent his son Ruocheng to give thanks in his place.

sentences.zh: 上以廷玉不親至，遂發怒，命降旨詰責。

translations.literal: Because Tingyu did not come in person, the emperor grew angry and ordered an edict issued rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Angered that Zhang Tingyu had not come in person, the emperor ordered an edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 軍機大臣傅恆、汪由敦承旨，由敦為乞恩，旨未下。

translations.literal: Grand Councilors Fu Heng and Wang Youdun received the instruction; Youdun pleaded for grace, but the edict had not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilors Fu Heng and Wang Youdun took the order; Youdun pleaded for leniency before the edict could issue.

sentences.zh: 又次日，廷玉入謝，上責由敦漏言，降旨切責。

translations.literal: Again the next day Tingyu entered to give thanks; the emperor blamed Youdun for leaking the words and issued an edict of sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The day after, Zhang Tingyu came to give thanks; the emperor blamed Youdun for leaking the order and issued a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請奪廷玉官爵，罷配享。

translations.literal: Court ministers requested stripping Tingyu of rank and title and abolishing his posthumous sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers asked that Zhang Tingyu be stripped of rank and denied posthumous enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 上命削伯爵，以大學士原銜休致，仍許配享。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the count's rank stripped, retirement with his original Grand Secretary title, and posthumous sacrifice still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped his count's rank, granted retirement with his original Grand Secretary title, and still allowed posthumous enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，皇長子定安親王薨，方初祭，廷玉即請南還，上愈怒，命以太廟配享諸臣名示廷玉，命自審應否配享。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year the heir apparent, Prince Ding'an, died; just as the initial sacrifice was held, Tingyu immediately asked to return south; the emperor grew angrier still and ordered the names of ministers granted Ancestral Temple sacrifice shown to Tingyu, commanding him to judge for himself whether he deserved sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year the heir apparent, Prince Ding'an, died; at the very first mourning rites Zhang Tingyu asked to return south; the emperor's anger deepened, and he showed Zhang Tingyu the roll of ministers enshrined in the Ancestral Temple and bade him judge for himself whether he deserved that honor.

sentences.zh: 廷玉惶懼，疏請罷配享治罪。

translations.literal: Tingyu, alarmed and fearful, memorialized requesting abolition of his sacrifice and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhang Tingyu memorialized asking that his enshrinement be revoked and that he be punished.

sentences.zh: 上用大學士九卿議，罷廷玉配享，仍免治罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, adopting the joint opinion of Grand Secretaries and the Nine Ministers, abolished Tingyu's sacrifice but still exempted punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, following the joint opinion of Grand Secretaries and Nine Ministers, revoked Zhang Tingyu's enshrinement but spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 又以四川學政編修硃荃坐罪，荃為廷玉姻家，嘗薦舉，上以責廷玉，命盡繳歷年頒賜諸物。

translations.literal: Also because Sichuan educational commissioner and reviser Zhu Quan was punished for an offense—Quan was related to Tingyu by marriage and had once been recommended by him—the emperor blamed Tingyu and ordered return of all objects bestowed over the years.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan educational commissioner Zhu Quan, a reviser related to Zhang Tingyu by marriage whom he had once recommended, was punished for an offense, the emperor blamed Zhang Tingyu and ordered return of everything the court had bestowed on him over the years.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，卒，命仍遵世宗遺詔，配享太廟，賜祭葬，諡文和。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year he died; an order was issued still to follow Shizong's testamentary edict enshrining him in the Ancestral Temple, with sacrificial and burial honors granted and posthumous title Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twentieth year he died; the emperor ordered that Shizong's edict be honored—enshrinement in the Ancestral Temple, full funeral honors, posthumous title Wenhe.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，上將臨雍視學，舉古禮三老五更，諮鄂爾泰及廷玉。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Qianlong reign, when the emperor was about to preside at the imperial school and inspect studies, he raised the ancient rite of the Three Elders and Five Worthies and consulted Oertai and Tingyu.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3, as the emperor prepared to preside at the imperial school, he revived the ancient rite of the Three Elders and Five Worthies and consulted Oertai and Zhang Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 廷玉謂無足當此者，撰議以為不可行。

translations.literal: Tingyu held that no one was adequate for this and drafted an opinion holding it impracticable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu held that no one was fit for the role and drafted an opinion against it.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，上撰三老五更說，闢古說踳駁，命勒碑辟雍。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year the emperor composed an exposition on the Three Elders and Five Worthies, refuting the ancient theory as confused, and ordered it carved on a stele at the Piyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year the emperor wrote an exposition on the Three Elders and Five Worthies, rejecting the old interpretation as confused, and ordered it carved on a stele at the Piyong.

sentences.zh: 五十年，復見廷玉議，以所論與上同，命勒碑其次，併題其後，謂「廷玉有此卓識，乃未見及。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he again saw Tingyu's opinion; because its arguments agreed with his own, he ordered it carved on a stele beside it and inscribed afterward, saying, "Tingyu had this keen insight, yet I did not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he came upon Zhang Tingyu's opinion again; finding it agreed with his own, he ordered it carved on a second stele with an inscription afterward: "Zhang Tingyu had this keen insight, yet I failed to see it.

sentences.zh: 朕必遵皇考遺旨，令其配享。

translations.literal: I shall certainly follow my late father's testamentary command and grant him sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: I shall certainly honor my late father's edict and grant him enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 古所謂老而戒得，朕以廷玉之戒為戒，且為廷玉惜之。」

translations.literal: What the ancients called guarding against complacency in old age—I take Tingyu's warning as my warning, and regret it for Tingyu as well."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients warned against complacency in old age—I take Zhang Tingyu's warning as my own, and regret what befell him."

sentences.zh: 終清世，漢大臣配享太廟，惟廷玉一人而已。

translations.literal: Throughout the Qing dynasty, among Han ministers granted Ancestral Temple sacrifice, Tingyu alone was so honored.
translations.idiomatic: Through the entire Qing dynasty, Zhang Tingyu was the only Han minister enshrined in the Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 子若靄，字晴嵐。

translations.literal: His son Ruowei, styled Qinglan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruowei, courtesy name Qinglan.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eleventh year of the Yongzheng reign.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Yongzheng 11.

sentences.zh: 廷試，世宗親定一甲三名。

translations.literal: At the palace examination the Shizong Emperor personally fixed the names of the first trio of the first class.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination Emperor Shizong personally selected the top three of the first class.

sentences.zh: 拆卷知為廷玉子，遣內侍就直廬宣諭。

translations.literal: When the papers were unsealed and it was known to be Tingyu's son, he sent a eunuch to the duty lodge to proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the papers were opened and his son was identified, the emperor sent a eunuch to the examiners' lodge with a message.

sentences.zh: 廷玉堅辭，乃改二甲一名，授編修，直南書房，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: Tingyu firmly declined; he was therefore changed to first place in the second class, appointed reviser, assigned to the Southern Study, and served as Grand Council secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu firmly declined; his son was placed first in the second class instead, appointed reviser, posted to the Southern Study, and made a Grand Council secretary.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，屢遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he rose to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 若靄工書畫，內直禦府所藏，令題品鑑別，詣益進。

translations.literal: Ruowei was skilled in calligraphy and painting; works in the imperial collection within the inner service he was ordered to inscribe, appraise, and distinguish—his refinement daily advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Ruowei excelled at calligraphy and painting; he was assigned to inscribe and appraise pieces in the imperial collection, and his skill steadily improved.

sentences.zh: 十一年，扈上西巡，感疾，歸卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, accompanying the emperor on the western tour, he fell ill and died after returning home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, while accompanying the emperor on a western tour, he fell ill and died after returning home.

sentences.zh: 若澄，字鏡壑。

translations.literal: Ruocheng, styled Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Ruocheng, courtesy name Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年進士，改庶吉士，直南書房，累遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of the Qianlong reign, transferred to Hanlin bachelor, assigned to the Southern Study, successively promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 10, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, served in the Southern Study, and rose to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 若澄亦工畫，亞若靄。

translations.literal: Ruocheng also was skilled in painting, second to Ruowei.
translations.idiomatic: Ruocheng also painted well, though less accomplished than Ruowei.

sentences.zh: 若渟，字聖泉。

translations.literal: Ruoting, styled Shengquan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoting, courtesy name Shengquan.

sentences.zh: 入貲授刑部主事，充軍機章京，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: By purchase of office he was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Justice, served as Grand Council secretary, and was twice promoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He bought his way into a secretship in the Ministry of Justice, served as Grand Council secretary, and was promoted twice to department director.

sentences.zh: 出為雲南澂江知府、四川建昌道。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Chengjiang in Yunnan and intendant of Jianchang circuit in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served abroad as prefect of Chengjiang, Yunnan, and intendant of the Jianchang circuit in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 內擢太僕少卿，五遷至侍郎，歷工、刑、戶諸部。

translations.literal: Recalled within, he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and five times promoted to vice minister, serving successively in the Ministries of Works, Justice, and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital he became vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and after five promotions reached vice-ministerial rank in the Ministries of Works, Justice, and Revenue in turn.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，授兵部尚書，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Jiaqing reign he was appointed Minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 he was made Minister of War, then transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，贈太子少保，賜祭葬，諡勤恪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; he was posthumously granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, sacrificial and burial honors were bestowed, and posthumous title Qinke.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died; he was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, granted funeral honors, and given posthumous title Qinke.

sentences.zh: 從子若溎，字樹穀。

translations.literal: His nephew Ruowei, courtesy name Shugu.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Ruowei, courtesy name Shugu.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年進士，授兵部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Yongzheng and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Yongzheng 8 and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 考選江西道御史。

translations.literal: He was selected by examination as a censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 擢鴻臚寺少卿，六遷刑部侍郎，擢​​左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, transferred six times to vice minister of the Ministry of Justice, and then promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, served six times as vice minister of Justice, and was then made left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上命旌卹勝朝殉節諸臣，若溎請遍行採訪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered honors and relief for ministers of the former dynasty who died loyal to their sovereign; Ruowei requested a thorough investigation throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered honors for Ming ministers who died loyal to their sovereign, Ruowei asked that a thorough investigation be conducted nationwide.

sentences.zh: 下大學士、九卿議，以為明史外兼採各省通志，專諡、通諡已至千五六百人，不必更行採訪。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers for deliberation; they held that besides the History of Ming, provincial gazetteers had also been consulted, and special and general posthumous titles already numbered fifteen or sixteen hundred persons, so further investigation was unnecessary.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries and Nine Ministers deliberated and held that beyond the History of Ming, provincial gazetteers had been used, and special and general posthumous titles already covered some 1,500–1,600 people, so further investigation was unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 若溎以老乞休。

translations.literal: Ruowei requested retirement on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: Ruowei retired on grounds of old age.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，屢迎謁。

translations.literal: When the emperor made southern tours, he repeatedly came out to welcome and pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's southern tours he repeatedly came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 五十年，與千叟宴，御書榜以賜。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders and was granted an imperially inscribed placard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders and received an imperially inscribed placard.

sentences.zh: 歸，又二年，卒。

translations.literal: He returned home, and two years later died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and died two years later.

sentences.zh: 論曰：世宗初即位，擢鄂爾泰於郎署，不數年至總督。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When Shizong first took the throne he promoted Oertai from a bureau post, and within a few years he reached governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: When Yongzheng first took the throne he promoted Oertai from a bureau post to governor-general within a few years.

sentences.zh: 廷玉已貳禮部，內直稱旨，不數年遂大拜。

translations.literal: Zhang Tingyu was already vice minister of the Ministry of Rites and pleased the emperor in inner service; within a few years he received the grand investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu was already vice minister of Rites and won favor in inner service; within a few years he was made grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 軍機處初設，職制皆廷玉所定。

translations.literal: When the Grand Council was first established, its offices and regulations were all set by Zhang Tingyu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Council was first established, Zhang Tingyu defined all its offices and procedures.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰稍後，委寄與相埒。

translations.literal: Oertai came slightly later, but the trust placed in him was comparable.
translations.idiomatic: Oertai came slightly later, but the trust placed in him was equal.

sentences.zh: 庶政修舉，宇內乂安，遂乃受遺命，侑大烝，可謂極心膂股肱之重矣。

translations.literal: Civil administration was well ordered and the realm was at peace; they then received the deathbed charge and were honored at the great sacrifice—one may say they reached the utmost weight of trusted ministers at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: With civil government well ordered and the realm at peace, they received the deathbed charge and were honored at the great sacrifice—truly they had reached the pinnacle of trust as the emperor's closest ministers.

sentences.zh: 顧以在政地久，兩家子弟賓客，漸且競權勢、角門戶，高宗燭幾摧萌，不使成朋黨之禍，非二臣之幸歟？

translations.literal: Yet because they had long been in power, the sons, clients, and guests of both families gradually competed for power and formed factions; Gaozong perceived the signs early and crushed the sprouts, preventing the calamity of cliques—is this not the good fortune of the two ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Yet after long years in power, the sons, clients, and guests of both families gradually competed for influence and formed factions; Qianlong detected the signs early and crushed them before factional disaster could arise—is this not the good fortune of both men?
